title: Uber (UBER) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
transcript:
Driver shortages in key emerging markets weighed on mobility results this quarter.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Wed, Nov. 4, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

TAKEAWAYS

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email[email protected]

RISKS

SUMMARY

Uber Technologies, Inc.(UBER+6.35%)reported growth for the third quarter of 2026, reaching 215 million monthly active platform consumers and delivering its fifth consecutive quarter of more than 20% gross bookings growth. Management noted that the company is shifting its autonomous vehicle strategy toward commercial execution, with plans to scale its driverless fleet to tens of thousands of vehicles by 2028. While international mobility growth faced headwinds from driver supply constraints in Brazil and India, the delivery segment saw accelerated organic growth supported by the expansion of the Uber One membership program. The company is currently integrating recent acquisitions such as EZCater and Blacklane to strengthen its premium and corporate offerings while focusing on organic expansion in its grocery and retail operations.

INDUSTRY GLOSSARY

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator:Hello, and welcome to Uber's Q3 26 Earnings Conference Call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question during this time, please press 1 on your telephone keypad. I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Wong, Head of Investor Relations. You may begin.

Alaxandar Wang:Thank you. Thank you for joining us today, and welcome to Uber's third quarter 26 earnings presentation. On the call today, we have Uber's CEO, Dara Khosrowshahi and CFO, Balaji Krishnamurthy. During today's call, we will present both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures, Additional disclosures regarding these non-GAAP measures, including a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP measures are included in the press release, supplemental slides, and our filings with the SEC. Each of which is posted to investor.uber.com. Certain statements in this presentation and on this call are forward looking statements. You should not place undue reliance on forward looking statements.

Actual results may differ materially from these forward looking statements and we do not undertake any obligation to update any forward looking statements we make today except as required by law. More information about factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from forward looking statements, please refer to the press release we issued today as well as risks and uncertainty described in our most recent Form 10 ks and in other filings made with the SEC. We published our quarterly earnings press release, prepared remarks, and supplemental slides to our Investor Relations website earlier today, and we ask you to review those documents if you have not already.

We will open the call to questions following brief opening remarks from Dara, With that, let me hand it over to Dara.

Dara Khosrowshahi:Thanks, Alex. Q3 was another strong quarter of growth and expanding profitability for Uber. With record audience and engagement across our platform. We reached 215 million monthly active platform consumers who are using Uber more frequently than ever. That helped us deliver our fifth consecutive quarter of 20+% year over year gross bookings growth alongside 35% growth in non-GAAP EPS and record trailing 12-month free cash flow of $10.4 billion. Mobility continued to see healthy growth but came in below our expectations as a result of driver supply not keeping pace with strong consumer demand, in several international markets. We are responding with targeted investments to improve driver availability and marketplace balance and we saw encouraging improvement in October.

Our focus is on driving consistent growth while maintaining strong profitability of the business. Delivery had another excellent quarter with gross bookings up 23% year-over-year, and organic growth accelerated. Our investments in selection, affordability and reliability are making Uber Eats even more useful for everyday occasions, from restaurant meals to weekly groceries and last minute essentials. And with approximately 55 million Uber 1 members, we are deepening consumer relationships across both mobility and delivery. Those direct consumer relationships are central to our approach to AI. We are using AI to make everyday transactions simpler, and discovery more personalized while selectively exploring new distribution channels that could bring incremental demand.

In AVs, our focus is shifting from partnerships and testing driverless commercial service. We are excited for Zoox to launch on Uber in Las Vegas later this month, with Motional moving up to fully driverless operations soon thereafter. We expect approximately 700 fully-driverless vehicles on Uber by year end, and more than 2,000 by the end of 27. Just as importantly, we are focused on demonstrating utilization and economics that are needed to scale. As we enter Q4, our priorities are clear. Improved mobility supply, build on deliveries momentum, and deliver against our AV milestones all while continuing to grow profitably.

Before I hand it off to the operator, I did also want to offer a special thanks to Jill Hazelbaker, our President and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer. After 10 years here at Uber, she's moving on to OpenAI. it is a big win for them. it is a loss for us to lose someone like Jill. She's been such a big part of our culture, our company. But fortunately, she has built a great team who gets to step up to more senior positions, many of them working with me directly. So I want to personally thank Jill for her 10 years here She's helped me in innumerable ways both professionally and personally as well.

She's been a great adviser. it is a big win for OpenAI. And I am really glad that the team that she built is ready to step up to bigger positions, which they fully deserve at the company. So big thank you to Jill. And with that, I will turn it over to the operator for questions.

Operator:Great. Thank you. Your first question comes from the line of Eric Sheridan with Goldman Sachs. Your line is open.

Eric James Sheridan:Thanks so much for taking the question. I want to come back to the parts of the letter and prepared remarks around EV fleet financing. Can you go a little bit deeper in terms of how we should be thinking about the balance sheet and incremental free cash flows that you want to put behind these efforts? And how should we be thinking about rates of return or aligning the economics with the commercial opportunity? Thanks so much.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:Thanks. Eric, I can take this. So I think, you know, we are not ready to say a lot on the structures that we are working on just yet. But what I would point you to is the $1 billion financing arrangement that we had set up with Santander earlier in the year, was focused on our traditional fleet partners That is a template for what we could be doing with our AV fleets as we go through the next few months. We are actively working on these kinds of setups. And, specifically, you should expect that we will have announcements to make both on infrastructure financing, but also on vehicle financing as we go forward.

So our long run expectation is that this should be financed by third party capital, not by Uber's balance sheet. And in the near term, as you have seen with the announcement, that we had in the release that people have about 700 driverless vehicles on our network this year. 2,000 by the end of next year. The capital deployment against those is fairly limited. But as we start scaling out into the 10 thousand+ in 2028 and beyond, we want to bring in third party capital again. That, and we feel good about the ROI that the third parties can get there.

Dara Khosrowshahi:And, Eric, just a little bit more for me, which is we do think that fleet financing for these cars is gonna be somewhat unusual in that you look at, fleet financing for rental car fleets, etcetera, they are all based on residual value of vehicles. And I think the residual value of the AV vehicles is not established yet. And so as a result, in the early days, we are gonna take these vehicles on our balance sheets. We have very strong balance sheet, are capable of doing so. And I think a lot of the fleet financing is gonna be based on revenue kind of revenue potential of these fleets.

And what we are able to demonstrate is that cars on our network get very, very high utilization and actually higher utilization on cars that are not on our network. You know, we show a 30% kind of utilization premium on our network. And we are able to do so very flexibly. So, you know, if there is a fleet that some reason fails in terms of their operations, we can take that AV vehicle and you know, put it under separate ownership, and it will still earn on the Uber network, so to speak. So we think that the financing on the Uber network can have a real advantage in terms of cost of capital versus alternatives.

And it is kind of a business model that we are working with to establish with partners. The reaction has been actually, you know, they are quite interested. They want to diversify away from. Centers, so to speak. So we are quite optimistic on it, but we do have to establish the business model, the utilization advantages, demonstrate that to the banks and then go from there.

Operator:Next question, please. Your next question comes from Nikhil Devnani with Bernstein. Bernstein. Your line is open.

Nikhil Devnani:Hey there. Thank you for taking the question. I wanted to follow-up on the international supply dynamic you called out. Just want to make sure, did something sort of change through the quarter? I think last time we had talked about Brazil. But it seems like there is a few more markets that are now reflecting this. So if you could just elaborate on what you saw through the quarter, would be helpful. Then also, as we look forward, should we be thinking about the supply side investments required Because some of the variables called out like immigration feel a little bit more persistent.

So it would be helpful to understand just the degree and persistence of these investments as you try and reaccelerate the business. Thank you.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:Yeah. Yeah. Thank you, Nikhil. So I think, what I would say is a lot of this is a continuation of the dynamics that we have seen through the year. And if you zoom out and, look at the macro environment, with the escalation and the war in The Middle East, fuel cost impacts have been felt, globally. Where it shows up most materially for us is in emerging markets where there is a level of price sensitivity on both the consumer and the driver side. And, what we talked about last quarter in Brazil was specifically focused on motor supply from delivery competition in the market.

But through the last quarter, we have seen the elevated fuel price impact in markets like Brazil and India in particular, quite meaningfully impacting the supply situation. Similarly, you know, the immigration dynamics have been in place through the year. But as we go through the back half of the year and we see elevated demand from the holiday season that you have coming through right now, which again, the demand picture is pretty strong. We see an elevated impact on the supply on the marketplace when the supply is short. So that is kind of what we are calling out Canada as well. Now, this is a good problem where we are at the scale that we are at.

Operating at, and we still are running into supply constraints rather than demand constraints. And we know exactly how to address those kinds of challenges with the history that we have demonstrated We are making targeted supply investments. So this is focused on driver acquisition, retention, and engagement. And as we go through that kind of investment, we are already encouraged with the early signs of supply that we saw in October, and supply hours growth globally accelerated in October. Including notable improvements in Brazil and India. So I think with all of that, you see our outlook is steady at the 18% to 22% growth range. Which is steady from the last couple of quarters.

So we feel good about where we are, and the growth runway in front of us is extremely long. Over the last 5 years, we have doubled our eligible benefit population penetration in our top 10 markets. But it is still at only 10%. Right? So we feel really good about where we can go from there.

Dara Khosrowshahi:I think just the additional factor that we are dealing with is that we obviously have year-over-year pressure on supply, but then we also have seasonal pressure on supply as well, which is September, October, November, December. are kind of peak season for us. for both mobility and delivery. And in some markets like Brazil, mobility and delivery depend on 2-wheel supply. Which for us is, for example, 1 of the examples of supply that we need to add So those kind of intermingle. So it is a it is a seasonal issue, and it is a year-on-year issue that are hitting together. But we have got a good handle on it.

We are very optimistic about the trends as we see them in October and going into Q4. And again, this is not the first time we have dealt with this kind of situation. Next question, please.

Operator:Your next question comes from Brian Nowak with Morgan Stanley. Your line is open.

Brian Thomas Nowak:Great. Thanks for taking my questions. Maybe 1 on grocery. Just talk to us a little bit philosophically about the investments you need to make in grocery and retail to sort of further accelerate and compete in that business in The U. S? How do you think about the need to have a larger 1P presence? So, you know, your own dark stores or your own sort of fulfillment operation.

Dara Khosrowshahi:Yeah. Absolutely, Brian. So we are very excited about the progress of our grocery and retail business. We are, you know, at a run rate now at a $15 billion run rate, growing 40% on a year-on-year basis. We think this is a $10 trillion TAM, so it is an enormous market for us. And what we see from consumers is over and over, is they want more stuff faster. They want everything faster. You know, I think when Amazon brought overnight shipping, it was it was magic. And now, you know, next-hour shipping is magic, and pretty soon people are gonna expect everything in 15 minutes. And we play right into that area.

The areas of investment for us are really about selection. They are about affordability. And they are about the consumer experience. You know, on the selection side, we are very excited to expand to Costco nationwide. We also have added a number of international players target Decathlon, Priceline in Australia, Tesco in The UK, Rui in Germany as well. So we continue to invest in selection. As we add selection, we have more consumers coming online as well. And also conversion rates improve. We continue to invest in affordability, whether it is fresh off Tuesdays or for example, members not having any fees above $60 that our members are loving as well.

And then we continue to invest in product innovation as well to make sure that know, our pick pack is as accurate as it can be shopper. We are investing in shopper quality, so we are paying high quality shoppers more, and we are also introducing technology, for example, where our shoppers will take a photo of an empty shelf to verify that the item that you are looking for is not there. It also helps our consumers because when they see the empty shelf, they do not get upset. it is not the shopper's fault. it is just what they wanted was not there. And so it helps establish trust between both sides of the marketplace.

So for us, it is just all about execution. You know, as it relates to dark stores, our number 1 priority has been to work with our partners and to help them grow their businesses, Now we are very excited as it relates to Delivery Hero. They have built a substantial quick commerce and dark store business. And the benefit of dark stores is that you have a much better handle on inventory Usually, your pick-and-pack success percentages. Your found rates are much higher, so quality goes up. As a result of the vertical integration. And, you know, this is a part of the delivery hero hopeful potential acquisition that we are very excited about.

That team is been building the quick commerce business for you know, well over, you know, 7 to 8 years. It has hit breakeven. It is growing at very attractive rates, and we are very excited to add that as part of our portfolio once we close on Delivery Hero. And just 1 additional comment on the dark store question.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:This is for us a fit-for-purpose sort of solution. Right? We will not we do not want to get into this business everywhere, but there are markets where it makes sense. As Dara mentioned, Delivery Hero has done a really good job with their dock store footprint in The Middle East. We are also in a position where we would be able to look at that business in Turkey both with our presence in the market, but also with the GATHER transaction that we have done. And that business, again, is running near profitability. And then we have organically experimented with this in Taiwan as well.

So, ultimately, it needs to be a business that can be run well, has to meet the market conditions, has to have a good return on assets when you go into that sort of field. We will be selective in where we engage with this. Otherwise, we would work with our grocery partners who are experts at doing that in their own space.

Operator:Next question, please. Your next question comes from Ronald Josey of Citi. Your line is open.

Ron Josey:Great. Thanks for taking the question. I want to ask a little bit more on the fully driverless rollout from 700 this year to 2,000 next year. Can you just help us understand a little bit on the geography pace of rollout? I think you said 50/50 in the U.S. and international and how you are thinking about that. Thank you.

Dara Khosrowshahi:Yeah. Absolutely. So, we are very excited. I mean, we have got launches. Obviously, we are in market with Waymo already in The US. We are in market with WeRide and Baidu. With no drivers, in a number of international markets. We expect to launch Zoox and Motional, as we mentioned, in Vegas this year. And then next year, we expect to add Nuro in California and then in Houston as well in Texas, at least early on in 2027. These are fully driverless commercial rides. and AV Ride in the middle of the year in Texas as well. And internationally, we expect to add Pony and Momenta to our no-driver vehicle operator kind of inventory.

In late 2027, I do think we are going to be doing kind of testing rides, vehicle operator testing rods with NVIDIA, with Rivian, hopefully, Waabi as well. And also Wayve outside of The US. So you know, they. The partner strategy and the panoply of all these partners are really going to start adding up, and we are quite confident of getting to 2,000 vehicles in 2027, but the real goal is to get to tens of thousands of vehicles in 2028 and beyond. And really scaling the ecosystem. And, you know, we are in market in these markets. We have relationships with the cities. We have operations in those markets. We do not have to build demand.

The demand is already there. So we think we can launch very quickly at very high utilizations for our partners which makes us even more optimistic about the opportunity here.

Operator:Next question, please. Sure. Your next question comes from Shweta Khajuria with Wolfe Research. Your line is open. Hello? Perhaps your line is on mute. Can you hear me? Yes, I can. Sorry about that.

Analyst:Thank you for taking my question. Let me try 2, please. The first is on AV unit economics. So in the illustrative example that you gave, 30% increase in paid trips, with a 23% decrease in fixed costs. And even if partners were to pay the transaction fee or take rate to Uber, that would still be that would still be additive to them. So my question is, how durable is that 30% increase in paid trips that you would add? How durable is that advantage as you think long term in AV? And then the second question I have is on just your capital allocation strategy. You talked about that in your letter. there is no change there.

In terms of your priorities, and you do not expect M&A further M&A until the year end or after. But I guess, how are you what was the rationale for EZCater How are you thinking about capital allocation in general when you think about mobility and delivery as well as AV going forward? Thanks a lot.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:Sure. Shweta. I will take the first 1. Dara is going to jump in on the second 1. So on the utilization lift, I would start by saying we believe it is a very durable advantage for Uber. And maybe just for context, when we are talking about the 30% lift here, we are comparing Uber's deployments on a hybrid, basis in the U.S. with mature 1P deployments. And these mature 1P deployments have the advantage of mix in that they include San Francisco, which is a uniquely favorable for AV deployments today. As that deployment scale broadens out, we expect that 1P deployments will likely have utilization that would be worse than what they are seeing in San Francisco.

And in fact, what you are seeing on the ground today is exactly that. Both for Waymo and Tesla, their trips per vehicle per day in the new markets that they have launched this year is in the low teens. Versus high twenties that we are seeing on our network in these hybrid markets. And effectively, you are looking at 100%-plus for us in those markets. I think the other part of this is we are also going to likely have advantages on additional pieces of the unit economics file First, the vehicle cost over time are going to come down. And that will be true for many players.

But in general, what we are trying to ensure here is that as we work with OEMs, we want to ensure that we have line of sight to advantaged pricing, that we can deliver because we have scale. Second piece that we will have, advantage on also is on shared charging, maintenance, and fleet infrastructure since that can be shared across multiple EV partners. And I would think about this as the hyperscalers getting an advantage versus on prem data centers that were serving 1 corporate. So I think those 2 pieces in addition to the utilization will support long term economics Our goal is for AV trips to deliver margins comparable to human driven trips over time.

And as we get beyond that point, we can share savings with consumers and truly expand TAM beyond what we are already seeing, on the ground.

Dara Khosrowshahi:Right. And in terms of, you know, capital allocation, etcetera, our priorities have not changed. Obviously, our number 1 priority is to drive organic growth. Investment in the AV ecosystem, we talked about a $10 billion commitment based on certain deliverables, both investment and partners. And or AV fleets, etcetera, that. that is another priority. And then there is m and a and buybacks as well, and we have plenty of capital for both. We are going to shift to, I would say, more of the top 2, and we are going to pull back on M&A. Chiefly because we are really focused on integration of the deals that we have already announced. The. Generally, their performance great.

But we wanna make sure we get the right cost of capital as it relates to M&A. And if you look at kind of our M&A philosophy historically and going forward, it is really in a couple categories. You know? 1, you will see deals that expand our geographies. Right? If they allow us to offer our services in more countries, Delivery Hero is an example of that. Trendyol is an example of that.

And not only do we get into new geographies that are growing very, very fast, but it allows us to offer the platform advantage, the power of the platform, which is mobility and delivery cross promoting each other, membership programs cross promoting each other, in more countries. So We are in many of the Delivery Hero markets, and it is just the extension of our platform geographically. The secondary reason we look at are what are capabilities that we can build that are specialized and we think really profitable. We talked about our premium business growing. and we have talked, for example; it is grown 35% year-on-year and our U4B business grew almost 50% year-on-year.

So premium is a theme for us and corporate business is a theme for us. Is something that we want to kind of double down on. And those, for example, are the acquisitions of Blacklane and EZCater that you asked about. You know, Blacklane gives us more specialty very high quality inventory, and EZCater has specialized capabilities. You know, they only work with merchant partners who focus on catering, A lot of times, the delivery partner has to come into the office, set things up. it is a different level of service.

And there is a huge advantage in being able to offer both Blacklane and EZCater to our U4B audience, which I think now we have got like half of Fortune 500 companies now as well. So those are established businesses. Different capabilities that we can introduce to our U4B audience and really embed with them even more. And then third is kind of new products that can grow with our audience. So Spot Hero is an example of that. We want our product to be more relevant, for example, to commuters. Commute is 1 of our largest categories.

And to be able to offer commuters, you know, and Uber to work, a pass to avoid surge, and parking if they want it when they want to drive is a great, for example, example for us building out our inventory of services to the commuter who is a top customer for us. So those are the themes that we are going after We are really excited about the acquisitions that we have on our books. We are very excited about EZCater, and generally as standalones, they are operating at higher levels than our deal cases, and now we would just wanna make sure that the integration is right. The teams are treated well.

And everything goes well, which is why next year, I think the focus is gonna be more on organic, autonomous, and then, of course, buying back stock. Opportunistically.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:I would just add that from a process-- sure. From a process standpoint, for any deals that you see us do, we are always evaluating the deal's 'buy' case. And we are looking at the accretion math relative to what it would look like if we just bought back our own stock. In this specific case, since you, asked specifically about EZCater, the build-versus-buy math could not be more, obvious. We are talking about acquiring a business that is profitable right now. We have more synergies coming. And relative to building this business, we expect that you would see a few hundred million-dollar profit swing in the build case versus buy.

So I think, you know, we feel very good about the logic, and we now are focused on executing against it.

Operator:Next question, please. Your next question comes from Michael Morton with MoffettNathanson. Your line is open.

Michael Morton:Good morning. Thanks for the question. I wanted to maybe talk about the potential combination of DoorDash and Instacart. Uber has talked a lot about the cross-platform you have experienced from your Eats to your mobility business. So I was wondering if you could talk about the potential opportunity and or risk that you see created by this combination. Thank you.

Dara Khosrowshahi:Yeah. Absolutely. So I do not think, honestly, Michael, it is gonna affect us too much. Our grocery and retail business is growing You know, it is a $15 billion run rate, growing 40%. Our focus really is to continue to improve the product, and the product still has a lot of improvement ahead of it in terms of selection, in terms of quality, in terms of on time rate, in terms of fill rates, etcetera. You know, when we talk to our merchant partners, they want choice. They wanna develop direct channels They want plenty of partners including us and DoorDash and Instacart to work with.

So this potential deal takes 1 of those partners off the table, and we have already had kind of reach-outs from our partners, you know, both who are very worried about the potential transaction and asking us, what do you think? and then 2, wanting to actually work with us more. Wanting to build their business with us so that they are not overly dependent on a single platform if DoorDash and Instacart happens, which will be a very, very large percentage of the online markets. But from our standpoint, the promise of this market is a $10 trillion market. You know, this would create a competitor that has big share of certainly the online, portion of that market.

But we think for us, we are gonna continue to invest in And, you know, these acquisitions create a lot of distractions. And at this point, the reach outs we have gotten from merchants are merchants who want to embed with us more deeply and wanna build their business with us. So that they have alternatives And, you know, it is gonna be up to the government to decide whether 1 alternative or 2 alternatives is better.

Operator:Next question, please. Your next question comes from Ken Gawrelski with Wells Fargo. Your line is open.

Analyst:Thank you. 2, if I may, please. First, could you talk about domestic or U.S. mobility trends, maybe what you saw in 3Q and in 4Q, you talked about improving mobility growth. But I want to see if we can touch a little bit upon what you are seeing in The U. S. Versus some of the international markets you have talked about. And in particular, I think there is a market focus on continued on California, maybe even in some markets in Texas where there is been heavier AV penetration. And the second question is, you talked about organic delivery acceleration. Could you talk about the drivers between kind of restaurants and grocery?

Are you seeing core restaurant acceleration as part of that overall organic acceleration. Thank you very much.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:Yeah. Thanks, Ken. On the U.S. for mobility, we are seeing relatively resilient growth in The US, versus the international trends we talked about earlier in the call. You know, growth moderated a bit in Q3, but not as much as in the international markets. You know, elevated gas prices are an issue globally, and there is some level of supply pressure that we are seeing in The US as well, but we are responding with the targeted investments, supply investments that we talked about. Earlier. I think beyond the supply question, what we are seeing in The US that continues to be true is the insurance tailwinds continue to build.

We talked about the meaningful acceleration in California trip growth. It continues to outperform relative to the rest of the country. 2, our barbell strategy on the product side continues to be really, really healthy in The US. US barbell products grew at 3x the rate of the overall business in Q3. And it is driven by strong innovation around growth that is portfolio in Wait and Save, Comfort, Reserve, Black, but then also to new demographics with teens and women preferences that are targeting just new cohorts of consumers and creating more options for our consumer base. And then finally, from a sparse market standpoint, we just see so much runway in The US.

Less than 10% of eligible consumers in sparse markets have used Uber in the last 12 months. That number in dense markets is 50% of consumers. So we continue to make improvements on supply and reliability in these markets, and that should have a long term impact that are very tangible. Dara, you wanna take the second 1?

Dara Khosrowshahi:Yeah. And we are quite pleased in terms of US delivery, which accelerated nicely. it is the second quarter in a row that organic growth and delivery and US delivery accelerated. And, really, it is for a number of factors. 1 is mathematically, our grocer and retail business and direct business which are growing faster than our OFD business, are becoming a higher percentage of the portfolio so to speak. So you just have kind of a bigger, faster growing part of the business getting even larger. Our core restaurant business is also accelerating, and that is because of really merchant selection, the number of merchants that we added in The US.

Was up nicely about 12% on a year-on-year basis. So as we add more selection, you know, everything helps conversion improves. We get new customers all on the platform as well. Membership is definitely a tailwind for us. So members are now 70% of delivery gross bookings. So membership is deepening in engagement with our consumers as well. And then, of course, sparse markets. As Balaji said, sparse markets is a play that we are running globally. But it is absolutely a play that we are running in The US as well for delivery. That helps And then last but not least, is really deals.

We are focused on kind of merchant-funded promotions in addition to the membership discounts that we give to our consumers. If you look at our ad business and merchant funded promotions, they grew to over $10 billion on a year-on-year basis. And, you know, these are dollars that we are giving to our consumers and the return for merchants is new consumers and kind of higher penetration in the marketplace. So all of it is working at this point.

If there is 1 issue, it is it runs with mobility and that we continue to invest in delivery and couriers to make sure that our courier growth keeps up with the consumer demand that we are seeing on the food side. That is right now the biggest challenge that we have got. But the team we think is more than up for it.

Operator:Question, please. Your next question comes from Mark Stephen Mahaney with Evercore. Your line is open.

Mark Stephen Mahaney:Hey. I just wanna ask 1 question on the profit profitability of the mobility segment, these 8% margins you had this last quarter. With the supply initiatives that you are introducing in international markets, does that mean you can maintain the profitability performance that you have had? Or is it-- do we have a detour? Is it structural, or is it a temporary detour? Or is there any detour just in those profit margins? Thank you.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:Yeah, Mark. I think well, I would just take you back to our philosophy as always, which is that we want to drive margin expansion for the total company on a year-on-year basis. And, ideally, we want to do the same for the segments as well. But on a quarterly basis, there is some variability in the business both from you know, just the investments we typically make in supply in holiday season, etcetera. So I do not.

I would not call out any kind of meaningful changes in the margin trajectory for the business, and, you know, we would have some color on just the Q4 supply investments for mobility that would have an impact on the take rate, but not necessarily from a margin standpoint, anything meaningful. Look. I think the final part I would make here is on profitability. You look at our outlook. We delivered a quarter of mid-30% EPS growth The Q4 outlook that we just provided at the midpoint is a 37% year-on-year growth on our non-GAAP EPS. So if anything, you are seeing the profit ramp, expand and that puts us in a pretty good spot for 2027.

SUMMARY

Uber Technologies, Inc.(UBER+6.35%)reported growth for the third quarter of 2026, reaching 215 million monthly active platform consumers and delivering its fifth consecutive quarter of more than 20% gross bookings growth. Management noted that the company is shifting its autonomous vehicle strategy toward commercial execution, with plans to scale its driverless fleet to tens of thousands of vehicles by 2028. While international mobility growth faced headwinds from driver supply constraints in Brazil and India, the delivery segment saw accelerated organic growth supported by the expansion of the Uber One membership program. The company is currently integrating recent acquisitions such as EZCater and Blacklane to strengthen its premium and corporate offerings while focusing on organic expansion in its grocery and retail operations.

Wanting to build their business with us so that they are not overly dependent on a single platform if DoorDash and Instacart happens, which will be a very, very large percentage of the online markets. But from our standpoint, the promise of this market is a $10 trillion market. You know, this would create a competitor that has big share of certainly the online, portion of that market.

But we think for us, we are gonna continue to invest in And, you know, these acquisitions create a lot of distractions. And at this point, the reach outs we have gotten from merchants are merchants who want to embed with us more deeply and wanna build their business with us. So that they have alternatives And, you know, it is gonna be up to the government to decide whether 1 alternative or 2 alternatives is better.

Operator:Next question, please. Your next question comes from Ken Gawrelski with Wells Fargo. Your line is open.

Analyst:Thank you. 2, if I may, please. First, could you talk about domestic or U.S. mobility trends, maybe what you saw in 3Q and in 4Q, you talked about improving mobility growth. But I want to see if we can touch a little bit upon what you are seeing in The U. S. Versus some of the international markets you have talked about. And in particular, I think there is a market focus on continued on California, maybe even in some markets in Texas where there is been heavier AV penetration. And the second question is, you talked about organic delivery acceleration. Could you talk about the drivers between kind of restaurants and grocery?

Are you seeing core restaurant acceleration as part of that overall organic acceleration. Thank you very much.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:Yeah. Thanks, Ken. On the U.S. for mobility, we are seeing relatively resilient growth in The US, versus the international trends we talked about earlier in the call. You know, growth moderated a bit in Q3, but not as much as in the international markets. You know, elevated gas prices are an issue globally, and there is some level of supply pressure that we are seeing in The US as well, but we are responding with the targeted investments, supply investments that we talked about. Earlier. I think beyond the supply question, what we are seeing in The US that continues to be true is the insurance tailwinds continue to build.

We talked about the meaningful acceleration in California trip growth. It continues to outperform relative to the rest of the country. 2, our barbell strategy on the product side continues to be really, really healthy in The US. US barbell products grew at 3x the rate of the overall business in Q3. And it is driven by strong innovation around growth that is portfolio in Wait and Save, Comfort, Reserve, Black, but then also to new demographics with teens and women preferences that are targeting just new cohorts of consumers and creating more options for our consumer base. And then finally, from a sparse market standpoint, we just see so much runway in The US.

Less than 10% of eligible consumers in sparse markets have used Uber in the last 12 months. That number in dense markets is 50% of consumers. So we continue to make improvements on supply and reliability in these markets, and that should have a long term impact that are very tangible. Dara, you wanna take the second 1?

Dara Khosrowshahi:Yeah. And we are quite pleased in terms of US delivery, which accelerated nicely. it is the second quarter in a row that organic growth and delivery and US delivery accelerated. And, really, it is for a number of factors. 1 is mathematically, our grocer and retail business and direct business which are growing faster than our OFD business, are becoming a higher percentage of the portfolio so to speak. So you just have kind of a bigger, faster growing part of the business getting even larger. Our core restaurant business is also accelerating, and that is because of really merchant selection, the number of merchants that we added in The US.

Was up nicely about 12% on a year-on-year basis. So as we add more selection, you know, everything helps conversion improves. We get new customers all on the platform as well. Membership is definitely a tailwind for us. So members are now 70% of delivery gross bookings. So membership is deepening in engagement with our consumers as well. And then, of course, sparse markets. As Balaji said, sparse markets is a play that we are running globally. But it is absolutely a play that we are running in The US as well for delivery. That helps And then last but not least, is really deals.

We are focused on kind of merchant-funded promotions in addition to the membership discounts that we give to our consumers. If you look at our ad business and merchant funded promotions, they grew to over $10 billion on a year-on-year basis. And, you know, these are dollars that we are giving to our consumers and the return for merchants is new consumers and kind of higher penetration in the marketplace. So all of it is working at this point.

If there is 1 issue, it is it runs with mobility and that we continue to invest in delivery and couriers to make sure that our courier growth keeps up with the consumer demand that we are seeing on the food side. That is right now the biggest challenge that we have got. But the team we think is more than up for it.

Operator:Question, please. Your next question comes from Mark Stephen Mahaney with Evercore. Your line is open.

Mark Stephen Mahaney:Hey. I just wanna ask 1 question on the profit profitability of the mobility segment, these 8% margins you had this last quarter. With the supply initiatives that you are introducing in international markets, does that mean you can maintain the profitability performance that you have had? Or is it-- do we have a detour? Is it structural, or is it a temporary detour? Or is there any detour just in those profit margins? Thank you.

Balaji Krishnamurthy:Yeah, Mark. I think well, I would just take you back to our philosophy as always, which is that we want to drive margin expansion for the total company on a year-on-year basis. And, ideally, we want to do the same for the segments as well. But on a quarterly basis, there is some variability in the business both from you know, just the investments we typically make in supply in holiday season, etcetera. So I do not.

I would not call out any kind of meaningful changes in the margin trajectory for the business, and, you know, we would have some color on just the Q4 supply investments for mobility that would have an impact on the take rate, but not necessarily from a margin standpoint, anything meaningful. Look. I think the final part I would make here is on profitability. You look at our outlook. We delivered a quarter of mid-30% EPS growth The Q4 outlook that we just provided at the midpoint is a 37% year-on-year growth on our non-GAAP EPS. So if anything, you are seeing the profit ramp, expand and that puts us in a pretty good spot for 2027.

Dara Khosrowshahi:And, Mark, just a little bit more so you understand the picture in terms of supply and demand. Know, we have base pricing for both kind of our consumer pricing and then base pricing for driver courier pay, etcetera. Then we have incentives. There are kind of, call it, rider side incentives, driver-side incentives, eater-side incentives, and then kind of courier incentives as well. These are more flexible dollars that we target times, like Halloween, to make sure drivers show up, etc. Or we will target places. If we think that there is a ball game going on, we will put incentives for drivers. To show up to the ballgame at the right time.

But the cool thing is that we just rebalance incentives between riders and drivers, for example, in this case. And so, whereas last year, more of the incentives went to riders to reduce price, Now this year, we are taking down rider incentives and we are using those dollars to fund driver incentives. Now that does mean sometimes higher prices for riders, which is something that we watch out for. We will do trade offs against profitability, but that is something that we handle. But there is a flexible incentive pool that we allocate to supply or demand based on the balance of the marketplace, and that is part of kind of the art that we have got.

And then there is a lot of science, algorithmic science that goes into hey. If you have a dollar, what is the maximum predicted return for that dollar? And should I invest that dollar in a driver in Brazil? Or should I invest that dollar in a rider in India, for example? And the algorithms are making these choices, and they structurally can make these choices based on, you know, training on billions of trips. And, you know, they can allocate these investments in a way that humans just cannot.

Operator:Thank you, Dara. Our last question, please? Your last question will come Douglas Anmuth with JPMorgan. Your line is open.

Douglas Till Anmuth:Thanks so much for the question. Hoping to get your latest thoughts on AI agents Can you just talk about some of the goals and differentiation that you can provide by building agent tech directly into the Uber platform? And then also how you are thinking about the opportunities on third party platforms like Mistral, and others. Thanks.

Dara Khosrowshahi:Yeah. Definitely. So, I think focus is making sure that we invest for the best possible experience by coming direct. You know? it is price, your delivery time, reliability, selection, Obviously, we have membership benefits, and members now account for more than 50% of our bookings. It just builds the best experience coming from direct. And we are really focused on making sure that the direct app experience is already frictionless. Right?

So, like, the mean ride time booking is less than a minute. it is actually 50 seconds. that is how much time people spend on our app, and 75% of our rides are single tap based on personalizing you know, your destination, based on the data that we have on you. You know, our mean-- if you look at the median time for an Eater to reorder, their favorite food, it is only 90 seconds. So we make sure that kind of coming to Uber does not require a bunch of toil. You can get in. You can get out.

And because of the data that we have, you know, where you are going, when you are going there, etc., we think we are gonna have a ton of people come direct to our site and listen, I used to work in the travel business, and we were dependent on the Googles of the world. I do not wanna go back there. So, really, kind of the best in class marketplace technology that we are building, operational execution, I think, is gonna have more and more people coming direct to us. And we are building our own AI experiences. You know?

For example, we have a cart assistant which we are very excited about, and early signal shows that baskets that you built with a card assistant are roughly twice the average of the average basket as well, and we are working on kind of each assistant, driver assistant, etc., to make sure that AI, we have the best AI systems that can get you in and out of our services very, very quickly. That said, we will have discussions with kind of third party AI agents. We think that it is another opportunity to reach our platform We think it will be a net positive in terms of demand into the ecosystem.

And you can guess based on kind of our services There are a lot of-- every single AI system company is talking to us, and we are really now negotiating the terms of trade. And the good news here is in most markets, you have 2 big mobility providers, 2 big delivery providers. You know, I think I have counted now. there are 8 different assistants, and I think there will be more than 10 assistants. So I think, you know, the content players in our space in the physical space, we are kind of the fulfillment. The demands on the services that we build are very large.

I think the demands on our services are to be very, very high. So something we are really excited about now it is pretty small.

Operator:Apologies.

Dara Khosrowshahi:I think you were telling me AI what were the transaction volumes at this point?

Balaji Krishnamurthy:Yeah. So I think just to put numbers to it, we had 1 of our largest weeks last week because it was Halloween. So we did just around 320 million trips on Uber and Uber Eats. The volumes coming from AI agents for Uber Eats were around 500. 500 orders total. And for our Rides business, it was a grand total of 4 trips that we have fulfilled from agents.

Dara Khosrowshahi:So it is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far. Listen, we hope that there will be more traction. Like, we do think that we wanna make services available to consumers in a delightful, easy way. we think our direct services are going to be the most delightful and easy, but we will work with third parties. it is just very, very early. And we wanna make sure we are not dependent on any 1 player. And I think we are very well positioned to in this environment going forward. All right. Well, I think that is it. Thank you everyone for joining.

Thank you Uber team for everything that you have done to deliver a great quarter. We are excited to close out the year with a really, really strong quarter, and a big thank you to our investors and our owners who put their dollars and faith in us as a company. More to come. Thank you.

Operator:This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for joining. You may now disconnect.
